title: Home Mortgage Loans: Monthly Interest, Full Installment Amount and Payoff Interest
content:
# Home Mortgage Loans: Monthly Interest, Full Installment Amount and Payoff Interest

This calculation guide explains how interest is measured on Home Mortgage Loans, what a full monthly installment consists of, and how interest is measured when a loan is paid off between installments.

## Calculation clauses

**Interest in arrears.** Interest is paid monthly and in arrears: each installment pays the interest that built up over the month behind it.

**Interest portion of an installment.** The interest portion of an installment is the unpaid principal as it stood after the previous installment, multiplied by the note rate and divided by 100, then divided by 12; the result is rounded half-up to the nearest cent.

**Full installment.** A full installment is the monthly principal-and-interest payment added to the monthly escrow payment.

**Payoff interest.** For a payoff, interest runs day by day starting from the due date of the most recent installment, with each day's interest equal to the unpaid principal multiplied by the note rate, divided by 100 and divided by 365.

**No prepayment penalty.** Paying principal early, in part or in full, never attracts a prepayment penalty.

## The same rules in tabular form

| Quantity | Base | Rate applied | Divisor | Rounding |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Monthly interest portion | principal remaining after the prior installment | note rate, as a percentage divided by 100 | 12 | half-up to the cent |
| Daily payoff interest | principal outstanding | note rate, as a percentage divided by 100 | 365 | not set by this policy |
| Full installment | principal-and-interest payment, together with the escrow payment | none | none | none |

## Worked examples (all figures hypothetical)

1. *Plain case.* Principal remaining after the prior installment is $200000.00 and the note rate is 6.000 percent. Multiplying $200000.00 by 6.000 and dividing by 100 gives $12000.00 for the year; dividing by 12 gives an interest portion of $1000.00.
2. *Half-up rounding.* Principal remaining is $100001.00 at 6.000 percent. The year's interest is $6000.06; dividing by 12 gives $500.005, which rounds half-up to $500.01.
3. *Full installment.* A loan with a principal-and-interest payment of $1432.25 and an escrow payment of $410.00 has a full installment of $1842.25.
4. *Payoff interest per day.* Principal outstanding of $150000.00 at 7.300 percent gives $10950.00 for a year; dividing by 365 gives $30.00 for each day of accrual since the last installment's due date.

These balances, rates and payments are invented for the examples and are not program rates.
